Task 10.0: Pilot Testing (M-3.10.1, M-3.10.2, M-3.10.3, M-3.10.4, EOP-A, EOP-B, EOP- C) Safety Testing and Commissioning The tests planned for safety and commissioning (Table 7) were informed by the outcomes of failure mode and effect analysis (FMEA) or Hazard and Operability Analysis (HAZOP). A HAZOP for a similar but larger scale system was done in co-ordination with the engineering, operation and health, safety & environment (HSE) team of a petroleum refinery customer. The HAZOP workshop also included consultants from a US-based engineering firm with extensive experience in industrial thermal systems. All safety tests were successfully completed. Both the vessel and piping circuit were pneumatically tested with nitrogen, meeting code requirements and receiving an ASME stamp after successful pressure testing. In response to expert feedback in Task 12, a third-party helium leak test with internal vacuum in the piping was conducted for a 30- minute dwell time, showing no leaks above 1×10⁻⁵ mbar·L/s. Hydrogen gas leak tests were performed on the pipe circuit at Element 16’s facility to verify weld joint integrity. During system commissioning, sulfur was loaded as solid pellets into the vessel and melted using the internal heat exchanger piping that circulates hot heat transfer fluid.
